claim: For a probability averaging measure and a finite real matrix family with square-integrable entries, the actual Bochner mean congruence equals congruence of the mean plus the centered covariance correction. The correction is PSD for PSD X, equals scalar variance times K1 X K1^T for square-integrable affine u, and has coefficient (b-a)^2/12 under actual normalized Lebesgue averaging on a nondegenerate interval.
assumptions: Probability measure nu and finite real matrix indices M,N.
Every K_ij is MemLp 2; PSD conclusion additionally assumes X.PosSemidef. Symmetry is unnecessary for the identity itself.
Affine specialization assumes square-integrable scalar u.
Uniform interval specialization assumes a<b and uses cond volume (Ioc a b), hence normalized Lebesgue measure.
dependency_graph: L2 entries imply L1 entries under the finite probability measure; each pair product is integrable by L2 Holder.
Scalar product covariance follows by expanding centered products and integrating all terms using derived integrability.
Finite sums of entry products yield the matrix identity with correct K_i,a X_a,b K_j,b orientation.
Matrix integrability is derived from entrywise integrability with Integrable.of_eval twice.
matrixMean_eq_integral uses eval_integral twice, identifying coordinate means with the actual Bochner matrix integral.
averaged_congruence_integral rewrites the coordinate result into direct Bochner integrals, using derived integrability for original and centered congruences.
Every centered congruence is PSD for PSD X; integration preserves symmetry and nonnegative quadratic forms.
For K0+u K1, the centered matrix is (u-Eu)K1, so correction is E[(u-Eu)^2] times K1 X K1^T.
The interval measure is inverse-length times restricted Lebesgue measure; mean is (a+b)/2 and polynomial integration gives variance (b-a)^2/12.

obligation_matrix.obligation: No integrability of the desired congruence or correction is assumed as an input: it is derived from hK.
The primary endpoint now uses actual Bochner integrals, not only an unconnected custom matrixMean operation.
The bridge uses the standard finite product topology and elementwise norm, whose Bochner integral agrees coordinatewise.
The local respectTransparency elaborator option resolves Matrix/Pi instance reducibility; it is not skipKernelTC or an untrusted computation.
No symmetry assumption is required for the identity; real PSD hypotheses are sufficient for the PSD correction.
The uniform variance uses actual normalized Lebesgue averaging and derives h^2/12, rather than assuming a variance oracle.
Rectangular K and zero-dimensional index sets are allowed; interval degeneracy is excluded by a<b.

residual_limits: No claim that averaging K itself gives the average quadratic action; the correction is essential.
The affine variance formula presumes scalar square integrability; the monograph should say this explicitly.
The uniform interval is nondegenerate; no density normalization is asserted at a=b.
